claims.text: THE QUALIFICATION, WHICH TRAVELS WITH THE ARTICLE AND IS ROUTINELY DROPPED. The description is what Lazar told the reporter, not an employment record. Stanton Friedman, who obtained the Los Alamos telephone directory page carrying Lazar's name, records that the page 'clearly states that it includes employees of the DOE and outside contractor, Kirk Meyer'. A Los Alamos colleague interviewed on tape by Mark Farmer on 25 May 1996 said Lazar 'was a contractor' under 'Kirk Mayer' and that he 'claimed to be' a physicist. Tom Mahood's 2018 conclusion is that Lazar worked as an electronic technician for Kirk-Mayer and that the Monitor article misrepresented his position on the basis of what he told the reporter.

claims.text: Bob Lazar's connection to the laboratory must be stated as 'named in a directory', never as 'employed by'. He appears in a 1982 Los Alamos telephone directory whose own text states that it covers Department of Energy employees and the outside contractor Kirk-Mayer; a colleague interviewed on tape in 1996 said Lazar 'was a contractor' under Kirk Mayer; and the laboratory later said it held no records for him. The Los Alamos Monitor of 27 June 1982 described him in the newspaper's own voice as 'a physicist at the Los Alamos Meson Physics Facility', which is what he told the reporter.

claims.text: A DISCREPANCY, NOT A RELATIONSHIP. The W-2 form in the Lazar literature is described as naming a 'Department of Naval Intelligence', which is not an entity that exists: the Office of Naval Intelligence sits inside the Department of the Navy. Stanton Friedman, who had seen the form, describes it only as 'His W-2 form from the Department of Naval Intelligence totals under $1000.00, at most a week's pay for a scientist.' Lazar's own 1991 narration says something different again: 'for the duration of my employment at S4 I was paid by the United States Navy'. THE FORM ITSELF WAS NOT OPENED BY THIS BOARD AND NO EMPLOYER IDENTIFICATION NUMBER, ZIP CODE OR BOX CONTENT IS ASSERTED ANYWHERE.

claims.text: THE CREDENTIAL CASE AGAINST LAZAR WAS MADE BY A UFO PROPONENT, NOT A DEBUNKER, AND THAT IS THE PART THE LITERATURE LOSES. Friedman, a nuclear physicist who spent his career arguing that UFOs are real craft, wrote 'The Bob Lazar Fraud' in December 1997, updated January 2011: 'No diplomas, no resumes, no transcripts, no memberships in professional organizations, no papers, no pages from MIT or Caltech yearbooks.' On the schools: 'Pierce said he had taken electronics courses in the late 1970s. The other three schools never heard of him.' On the professor Lazar named as a Caltech instructor: 'I located Dr. Duxler. He's a Pierce Junior College physics prof, and never taught at Caltech.' Duxler checked his own records and told Friedman that Lazar had taken at least one of his Pierce classes in the late 1970s.
